voiceDialog.title: Set Up Table Read Voices
voiceDialog.introDevice: Table Read can use the voices installed on this device, or an AI voice provider with your own API key.
voiceDialog.introBrowser: Choose how Table Read speaks in the browser: with the voices installed on this computer, free, or with an AI voice provider and your own API key.

voicePicker.setUpProvider: Set up an AI voice provider…
voicePicker.missingHint: That voice is not installed here, so an automatic voice reads instead.

macros.noneNew: No new macros in that file.
macros.title: Macros
macros.description: Text you type often — CONTINUOUS, LATER, a location you keep coming back to — inserted with a shortcut or from Edit → Insert Macro. With an element type, a macro turns an empty line into that element, or adds a new one after the current line.
macros.clashElementMenu: This shortcut is also used by the element menu; only the first one will run.
macros.clashMacro: This shortcut is also used by another macro; only the first one will run.
macros.footerHintMac: Shortcuts need at least one of ⌘, ⌥ or ⌃. A shortcut the editor already uses (bold, element types) keeps doing that instead. Macros are kept on this device; use Export and Import to move them to another.
macros.footerHintOther: Shortcuts need at least one of Ctrl or Alt. A shortcut the editor already uses (bold, element types) keeps doing that instead. Macros are kept on this device; use Export and Import to move them to another.

grammar.blurbGrammar: Real grammar mistakes: agreement, tense, articles, capitalization, repeated words.
grammar.blurbStyle: Wordiness and tone suggestions (passive voice, weak intensifiers, "in order to").
grammar.title: Grammar & Spelling Settings

saving.pickerFailed: Could not open the folder picker: {{error}}
saving.title: Saving
saving.description: Choose whether OpenDraft saves your work on its own. With auto-save off, nothing is written until you choose Save. OpenDraft asks before you close a script, open another one or close the window. A recovery copy is still kept in case the app quits unexpectedly.
saving.library: Auto-save scripts in my OpenDraft library
saving.libraryHint: Including scripts saved to a project folder or with Save to File As — each save updates their file too.
saving.filesHint: Each save writes over the original file. A Final Draft or Fountain file can only keep what its format supports, so notes and other OpenDraft-only details are not saved into it.
saving.projectFoldersDesc: A project can be kept in a folder on disk — a RAID, a network drive, a folder you already use. Each script is saved there as its own file, so the latest version is always in that folder. OpenDraft keeps a working copy too, for versions, notes and images.
saving.newProjectsHint: You can still choose for each project when you create it.
saving.projectsFolderHint: Each new project gets a folder of its own inside this one.
saving.oneDrive: This folder is inside OneDrive. That works, but if a script is edited on two computers before OneDrive syncs, OpenDraft will ask which version to keep.
saving.fileFormatHint: .odraft keeps everything. Final Draft and Fountain files open in other apps, but notes, tags and other OpenDraft-only details are kept only in OpenDraft's working copy. Treatments are always saved as .odraft.

voice.confidentiality: Confidentiality warning. AI voices send the text of your script to {{provider}} to be spoken. This may breach your data security or confidentiality obligations — an NDA, a studio’s policy, or your own rules for unreleased work. OpenDraft does not guarantee the confidentiality of anything sent to a third-party provider.
voice.confidentialityGemini: On Gemini’s free tier, Google may use what you send to improve its products, and human reviewers may read it.

providers.kokoro: Kokoro — free, runs on this device

cost.kokoro: Free, with no account. English voices only.
cost.gemini: Free tier with a Google account (with daily limits); paid tier billed by Google.
cost.openai: Paid, billed by OpenAI per character.
cost.elevenlabs: Small free allowance each month; paid plans beyond it.
cost.azure: Free tier of 500,000 characters a month; paid beyond it.
cost.compatible: Whatever your server costs — free when it runs on your own machine.

voice.useSystemDevice: Use the voices installed on this device
voice.useSystemComputer: Use the voices installed on this computer
voice.systemHintApp: Installed voices are free and work offline. AI voices sound more natural, need an account with the provider, and are billed by them.
voice.systemHintBrowser: Installed voices are free. AI voices sound more natural, need an account with the provider, and are billed by them.
voice.systemHintBrowserExtra: Which installed voices you get depends on the browser; some also add online voices of their own (Chrome’s “Google” voices), which send the text to that company to be spoken.
voice.kokoroApp: Kokoro runs inside the app on this device; your script is not sent to any AI provider. The first read downloads the voice model from Hugging Face and keeps it for next time: about 330 MB where the device’s graphics chip can run it (WebGPU), which reads fast, or about 90 MB otherwise, which is slower than speech and pauses between lines.
voice.kokoroBrowser: Kokoro runs inside this browser on this device; your script is not sent to any AI provider. The first read downloads the voice model from Hugging Face and keeps it for next time: about 330 MB where the device’s graphics chip can run it (WebGPU), which reads fast, or about 90 MB otherwise, which is slower than speech and pauses between lines.
voice.apiKeyOptional: API key (if your server needs one)
voice.createAzure: Create a Speech resource in the Azure portal
voice.keyKeptApp: The key is kept only on this device and sent only to {{provider}}.
voice.keyKeptBrowser: The key is kept only in this browser and sent only to {{provider}}.
voice.geminiHint: Gemini takes each character’s parentheticals and Speech Pattern as directions for how to say their lines.
voice.regionHint: The region of your Speech resource, shown with its keys in the Azure portal.
voice.serverAddressHint: The address up to and including /v1 of a server that offers OpenAI’s /audio/speech API — Kokoro-FastAPI, OpenedAI Speech, LocalAI and others.
voice.voicesPlaceholder: Leave empty to ask the server
voice.voicesHint: Comma-separated voice names, if the server cannot list its own.

addOns.privacyUnknown: This add-on has not said whether it sends anything off your device.
addOns.turnOffDesc: Its menu items and panels are removed straight away. You can turn it on again at any time.
addOns.forget: Also delete its saved settings, such as a server address or API key
addOns.title: Add-ons
addOns.description: Optional features you can choose to use. Each one is off until you turn it on, and nothing it does reaches your scripts — or leaves your device — before then.

dictionaryLibrary.empty: No dictionaries yet. Create one above.

dictionaryConfig.removeConfirm: Remove "{{name}}" from this installation? You can re-download it any time.
dictionaryConfig.languagesDesc: Hunspell engines that check words. Enable any combination for this script.
dictionaryConfig.installerDesc: Languages are downloaded from jsdelivr (wooorm/dictionaries) or the LibreOffice dictionaries repo on GitHub, and cached locally. A network connection is required for the first install.
dictionaryConfig.customUrl: Install from custom URL (e.g. Hindi, Tamil, etc.)
dictionaryConfig.customUrlDesc: Paste links to a Hunspell `.aff` and `.dic` file. The pair will be downloaded and cached locally.
dictionaryConfig.projectEmpty: No words yet — anything you "Add to Dictionary" goes here by default.
dictionaryConfig.projectDisabled: Disabled for this project — checks skip these words and "Add to Dictionary" routes to globals only.
dictionaryConfig.globalDesc: Reusable word lists shared across projects. Enable any combination for this script.
dictionaryConfig.globalEmpty: No global dictionaries yet. Click "Manage library…" to create one.
dictionaryConfig.flagProperNounsDesc: When off, capitalized unknown words (names, places, brands) are not flagged. Turn on for stricter checking — real proper nouns will then need to be added to a dictionary.
dictionaryConfig.intro: Configure which dictionaries are active for this script and where "Add to Dictionary" sends new words.

account.title: Account & Security
account.description: Manage your password, devices, two-factor verification, and account deletion.
account.twoFactorHint: When on, signing in from a new device requires a 6-digit code emailed to you. When off, you'll only get a heads-up email so you can spot unauthorized sign-ins.
account.smtpMissing: Email is not configured on this server, so verification codes can't be sent. Two-factor verification is unavailable until SMTP is set up.
account.changePasswordHint: Updating your password will sign you out everywhere. You'll need to sign in again with the new password on each device.

language.title: Language
language.description: The language of menus, dialogs and messages. Your scripts and exports are not changed.

printing.title: Printing
printing.description: What File → Print sends to the printer.
printing.viaPdf: Print the PDF, so the pages match the ones on screen
printing.viaPdfHint: The editor draws its page turns rather than making them, so printing the page asks the browser to lay the script out a second time — and it can end its pages somewhere else. Printing the PDF gives the pages you have been looking at, and the same document anyone you send the export to would read. Turn this off to use the browser's own print dialog instead, which is quicker on a long script and is what its margin and scaling controls apply to.

wordExport.title: Word Export
wordExport.description: How File → Export → Word writes your script.
wordExport.exactHighlightsHint: Off: highlights become Word's own highlights, in the nearest of Word's colors, so Word's highlighter can remove or change them. On: every highlight keeps the exact color you picked, but Word treats it as shading behind the text rather than a highlight. To remove it in Word, use Borders and Shading → Shading → Fill: No Color.

tableRead.title: Table Read Voices
tableRead.descriptionDevice: The voices Tools → Table Read uses to read the script aloud: the ones installed on this device, or an AI voice provider. Each character’s voice is chosen on their profile in the Characters panel.
tableRead.descriptionComputer: The voices Tools → Table Read uses to read the script aloud: the ones installed on this computer, or an AI voice provider. Each character’s voice is chosen on their profile in the Characters panel.

editing.title: Editing
editing.description: How the editor responds while you write.
editing.menuOnEnter: Offer the element menu when I press Enter on a blank line
editing.menuOnEnterHint: On a blank line, Enter opens a menu of element types. Press Enter again — or choose Blank Line — to keep the blank line instead. Turn this off to make Enter always insert a plain line.
editing.shortcutHintMac: Opens the element menu wherever the cursor is, on a blank line or a line with text. This is the way to it if you turn the setting above off. Click the box and press the keys you want; the combination needs at least one of ⌘, ⌥ or ⌃.
editing.shortcutHintOther: Opens the element menu wherever the cursor is, on a blank line or a line with text. This is the way to it if you turn the setting above off. Click the box and press the keys you want; the combination needs at least one of Ctrl or Alt.

smartType.title: SmartType lists
smartType.description: Add, edit, remove or reorder suggestions with one item per line. Save lists to apply changes. Entries use uppercase and duplicates are removed. These lists stay on this device.
smartType.hint: Names, locations, times and transitions already used in the current script are still suggested. Clearing a list removes its saved suggestions; it does not change your script.

scenePrefixes.label: Scene prefixes / intros
scenePrefixes.hint: For example INT., EXT., or DREAM SEQUENCE:. A space is added after each prefix.

times.label: Scene times
times.hint: For example DAY, NIGHT, or MAGIC HOUR.

characterExtensions.label: Character extensions
characterExtensions.hint: For example V.O. or THROUGH PHONE. Parentheses are added automatically.

transitions.label: Transitions
transitions.hint: For example CUT TO: or FADE TO WHITE:. Include the punctuation you want inserted.

smartType.saved: SmartType lists saved on this device.
smartType.saveFailed: Could not save SmartType lists: {{message}}. Your changes are still here; try saving again.
